title: Surge affinity, soft-stepdown reclaim, and invoice-smoothing policy for temporary boosts
creator: Jamal Ortiz
description:
Problem: Customers using Dedicated capacity sometimes trigger short-lived spikes (5m-2h). Current surge pools allow temporary boosts but lead to sharp overage charges and noisy operator interventions. We need a mechanism that preserves latency guarantees for bursty tenants while reducing invoice surprises and making reclaim behavior predictable to both customers and operators.

Goals:
- Provide a deterministic 'surge affinity' window so a tenant's temporary boost remains close to their original fleet (improves cache locality and latency).
- Implement a soft-stepdown reclaim policy that gently reduces boosted capacity over a configurable grace window instead of immediate preemption.
- Add an invoice-smoothing algorithm (30/60/90min bucketing) tied to boost lifecycle to amortize short spikes and avoid per-minute overage shock.
- Surface clear signals in the Console and operator runbooks for when soft-stepdown transitions to hard reclaim.

Proposed design (high level):
1) Surge affinity: when a boost is allocated from a surge pool, annotate allocation with affinity token and preferred node-group ID. For the affinity window (configurable, default 15m) router favors same node-group for subsequent requests. This improves KV cache hit-rate for the burst.
2) Soft-stepdown reclaim: introduce a reclaim state machine with states {BOOSTED, SOFT_STEPDOWN, HARD_RECLAIM}. Transition to SOFT_STEPDOWN begins when pool utilization crosses sustained threshold for > grace_period (default 10m). In SOFT_STEPDOWN we reduce per-tenant allowed qps by 20% every interval (default 3m) for up to xxx intervals, allowing client retries and autoscaler to warm up. HARD_RECLAIM force-evicts KV cache after final interval.
3) Invoice smoothing: implement billing sampler which records boost intervals and applies an exponential decay window (30/60/90min) to compute billable overage. Short blips under 10min get 0% billable for first 10m; remaining usage amortized. Configurable per-contract.
4) Console + operator UX: new panels in Console: Boost Timeline, Affinity Heatmap, Stepdown Forecast and Estimated Invoice Impact. Operator runbook and Slack alert flows when SOFT_STEPDOWN enters interval 1 and when HARD_RECLAIM scheduled.

Acceptance criteria:
- Router honors affinity tokens 95% of time during affinity window (measured in canary with 50 tenants).
- KV cache hit-rate for boosted requests improves by >= 10% vs baseline.
- Soft-stepdown triggers predictable reductions with test harness showing gradual qps rampdown across 3 intervals.
- Invoice smoothing reduces short-blip invoice spikes by >= 50% for synthetic workload (random 2-20m bursts).
- Console surfaces Boost Timeline and operators can manually escalate/rollback boosts.

Implementation plan (milestones):
- Week 1: Proto design doc + Confluence spec; router affinity token plumbing; storage schema for boost metadata.
- Week 2: Soft-stepdown state machine in surge controller; unit tests; simulation harness.
- Week 3: Billing sampler and offline invoice-smoothing batch job; integrate with billing pipeline; run backfill test.
- Week 4: Console panels and operator runbook + canary rollout to 10 customers.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Affinity increases allocation stickiness; could reduce global utilization if too long. Mitigation: elastic affinity expiry and forced migration after configurable max age.
- Soft-stepdown delays reclamation which may increase peak costs. Mitigation: per-tenant cap and fast-path hard reclaim for emergencies.
- Invoice smoothing introduces non-linear billing rules that require legal approval and clear UI language. Coordinate with finance and legal.

Telemetry and metrics to add:
- boost.allocations.total, boost.allocations.affinity_hit_rate, boost.stepdown.transition_times, boost.qps.reduction_profile, billing.smoothing.adjusted_overage, operator.actions.invocations

Docs and artifacts:
- Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/RED-2032-Surge+Affinity+and+Soft+Stepdown (initial draft)
- Design diagrams: Google Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1-BurstAffinityDraft
- Simulation harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/surge-sim (PR TBD)

Testing plan:
- Unit + integration tests for controller state machine.
- Load simulation with mixed steady/bursty tenants (100 tenants, random bursts) to validate stepdown and affinity effects.
- Billing backfill run against last 30 days of test cluster logs to compute invoice deltas.

Rollout plan:
- Canary group (10 customers, low-risk): enable affinity + soft-stepdown but keep billing smoothing off. Collect metrics 72h.
- If stable, enable billing smoothing in a separate deployment and monitor invoice deltas for 7 days.
- Gradual ramp to 50% of dedicated fleets; provide customer opt-out flag on contract page.

Operator runbook (abridged):
- Alert: SOFT_STEPDOWN_ENTER (severity medium) -> check Boost Timeline -> if unexpected, escalate to oncall infra.
- If HARD_RECLAIM pending and customer complains, operator can issue temporary grace extension from Console (+30m).

Notes: coordinate with Billing (Elena Park), Legal (Rajiv Mehta), and Console (Priya Rao) for messaging and toggles.
